(a) Extension.—Notwithstanding section 2002 of the Military Construction Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2011 (division B of Public Law 111–383; 124 Stat. 4436), the authorization set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2301 of that Act (124 Stat. 4444), shall remain in effect until October 1, 2014, or the date of the enactment of an Act authorizing funds for military construction for fiscal year 2015, whichever is later. 
    (b) Table.—The table referred to in subsection (a) is as follows:Air Force: Extension of 2011 Project Authorization





StateInstallation or LocationProjectAmount
BahrainSouthwest AsiaNorth Apron Expansion$45,000,000

fable.w: This section only extends the life of an existing military construction project authorization for an Air Force project in Bahrain. There is no real tempting reading: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any decision. The mention of a future Act authorizing funds refers to Congress, which is inside the federal government.
fable.s: the authorization set forth in the table in subsection (b), as provided in section 2301 of that Act (124 Stat. 4444), shall remain in effect until October 1, 2014

opus.w: This section only extends how long an earlier Air Force construction authorization (North Apron Expansion in Bahrain) stays in effect. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. "State" here is just a column heading in a table and does not mean state governments are taking part.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple appropriation authorization for a military construction project. It lists the location, project name, and cost but contains no language requiring or recommending consultation, coordination, or input from any outside parties (such as the government of Bahrain, local communities, or experts) before the decision is made. The decision-making process described is entirely internal to the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Air Force: Extension of 2011 Project Authorization... Bahrain... South Apron Expansion... $45,000,000
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the project is in Bahrain, it involves foreign entities or local governments, implying participation. However, the text only lists the location and amount; it does not describe any process of consultation, coordination, or input from outside parties (foreign or domestic) in the decision-making process. The authorization is purely internal to the federal government (Congress authorizing funds for the Air Force).
